STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r9.claim: The surah is a major Quranic treatment of nature's spiritual significance.
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r9.anchor: This sūrah is one of the most important of those in the Quran that point out the spiritual significance of nature.

STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r10.claim: It surveys nature's wonders and blessings, including livestock, crops, celestial bodies, the sea, mountains, streams, and landmarks for travel.
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r10.anchor: Substantial parts of this sūrah are devoted to the wonders of the natural world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verse directs readers to the implications of monotheism and accountability in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This verse directs attention to the consequences of belief in one God and in the accountability of the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Idolaters acknowledged God as Creator yet shared His rights with creatures, thereby equating Creator and created.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: would make them share His rights and in this way equate the creator with His creatures.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r8.claim: The Creator is unlike idols and other worshiped beings that create nothing, so worship belongs to the one who originates creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r8.anchor: ذكر تعالى التباين بين من يخلق وهو الباري تعالى، وبين من لا يخلق وهي الأصنام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r9.claim: The second من may include rational and irrational objects of worship, reflect the pagans' belief in idols' effects, parallel من يخلق, or restrict the comparison to beings with understanding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r9.anchor: وجيء بمن في الثاني لاشتمال المعبود غير الله على من يعقل وما لا يعقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r10.claim: The comparison argues that if even rational non-creators differ from the Creator, idols without even the attributes of living beings are still less worthy of worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r10.anchor: فإذا وقعت البينونة بين الخالق وبين غير الخالق، من أولي العلم فكيف بمن لا يعلم البتة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why the argument does not reverse the comparison, then answers that idolaters made God resemble creatures by equating them in naming and worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r11.anchor: قال الزمخشري: (فإن قلت) : هو إلزام للذين عبدوا الأوثان وسموها آلهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r12.claim: The rebuke أفلا تذكرون says this distinction should not be overlooked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r12.anchor: ثم وبخهم بقوله: أفلا تذكرون، أي: مثل هذا لا ينبغي أن تقع فيه الغفلة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r7.claim: The full arrangement and clarity of the signs leaves no doubt that Allah alone is Creator, given His oneness, knowledge, power, and wisdom, the signs' universal benefit, and idols' incapacity.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r7.anchor: لما لم يبق - بذكر الدلائل على الوحدانية على الوجه الأكمل , والترتيب الأحسن , والنظم الأبلغ - شبهة في أن الخالق إنما هو الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r8.claim: Differences in existence and qualities where no cause except choice explains them show that God acts by choice and can bring about whatever He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r8.anchor: للمفاوتة في الوجود والكيفيات بين ما لا مقتضى للتفاوت فيه غير الاختيار , فثبت بذلك أنه قادر على الإتيان بما يريد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r9.claim: The rhetorical comparison asks whether the One who continually creates as He wills can be like idols, which never create and are therefore contingent and incapable.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r9.anchor: يجدد ذلك حيث أراد ومتى أراد فلا يمكن عجزه بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r10.claim: Reversing the comparison would lose the force of lowering the higher party to the incapable idols' level and thereby rebuking their worshippers.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r10.anchor: ولو كان التشبيه معكوسا كما قيل لم يفد ما أفاد هذا التقدير من الإبلاغ في ذمهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r11.claim: Calling the idols 'who' treats them as if they were rational because their worshippers named them gods; if they fail at creation, their divinity is all the more impossible.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r11.anchor: وعبر ب ( من ) لأنهم سموها آلهة , وأنهى أمرها أن تكون عاقلة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r12.claim: The closing question urges reflection on the visible evidence, even from some angles, so people will abandon associating partners with God.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r12.anchor: حثا لهم على التذكر المفيد لترك الشرك

FARRA:v2p97/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p97/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p97/r7.claim: من may refer to a nonhuman in أفمن يخلق because the created entity is paired with the Creator; the phrase about animals also uses من, and Arabic uses it for a rider and his mount when treated together.
FARRA:v2p97/r7.anchor: جعل (من) لغير الناس لما ميزه فجعله مع الخالق وصلح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r4.claim: God's greatness means worship belongs to Him alone, unlike idols that create nothing and are themselves created.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r4.anchor: وأنه لا تنبغي العبادة إلا له دون ما سواه من الأوثان، التي لا تخلق شيئا بل هم يخلقون

MUQATIL:16:14-17/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r6.claim: The Creator of all the preceding things is unlike idols such as al-Lat, al-Uzza, Manat, and Hubal, which create nothing; people should reflect and affirm God's oneness.
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r6.anchor: هذه الأشياء من أول السورة إلى هذه الآية، { كمن لا يخلق } شيئا من الآلهة: اللات، والعزى، ومناة، وهبل

THALABI:v6p12/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p12/r6.claim: The creator, God, cannot be compared with idols that create nothing; the comparison calls people to remember.
THALABI:v6p12/r6.anchor: أفمن يخلق يعني الله تعالى كمن لا يخلق يعني الأصنام أفلا تذكرون

THALABI:v6p12/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p12/r7.claim: He links the argument to the verses challenging people to show what other gods created.
THALABI:v6p12/r7.anchor: نظيرها قوله تعالى: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه وقوله عز وجل: أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r6.claim: In the question about who creates, the intended creator is God Himself.

SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r1.claim: If this means all things worshipped besides God, من is apt because rational beings dominate the mixed class; ما would also be permissible.
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r1.anchor: إن أريد ب " من لا يخلق " جميع ما عبد من دون الله كان ورود " من " واضحا

SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r2.claim: For idols, من may treat them as rational beings because worshippers regard them as able to harm and benefit; the bird-flock poem also uses من for birds.
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r2.anchor: أسرب القطا هل من يعير جناحه

SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r3.claim: A second explanation for applying من to idols is syntactic correspondence with the preceding من يخلق.
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r3.anchor: الثاني: المشاكلة بينه وبين من يخلق

SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r4.claim: A third explanation reserves من for rational beings: if rational non-creators are unworthy of worship, lifeless idols are still less worthy; the cited challenge is 7:195.
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r4.anchor: تخصيصه بمن يعلم، والمعنى: أنه إذا حصل التباين بين من يخلق وبين من لا يخلق من أولي العلم

SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r5.speaker: قطرب
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r5.claim: On Qutrub's view that من may refer to non-rational things under a condition, its use here needs no further explanation.
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r5.anchor: إيقاع " من " على غير العقلاء من شرط كقطرب فلا يحتاج إلى تأويل

SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why the wording does not instead ask whether a non-creator is like the Creator, if idolaters equate idols with God.
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: هو إلزام للذين عبدوا الأوثان ونحوها

SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers that by naming and worshipping idols as God, idolaters made them like God and hence like created things; the verse rejects this.
SAMIN-DURR:16:17/r7.anchor: حين جعلوا غير الله مثل الله لتسميتهم باسمه، والعبادة له، جعلوا من جنس المخلوقات وشبيها بها

ASAD-NOTES:16:17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:17/r1.claim: The creator cannot be equated with beings unable to create, a contrast meant to prompt reflection.
ASAD-NOTES:16:17/r1.anchor: IS, THEN, HE who creates comparable to any [being] that cannot create?

QIRAAT-ER:16:17:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:17:10#1/r1.speaker: Assim
QIRAAT-ER:16:17:10#1/r1.claim: Assim fully assimilates tāʾ into dhāl in tadhdhakkarūna; the two forms are canonical variants with no stated semantic difference.
QIRAAT-ER:16:17:10#1/r1.anchor: Assim, mutawatir: Full assimilation of tāʾ into dhāl — tadhdhakkarūna vs tadhakkarūna; both are canonical 7-reader variants

ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r1.claim: The creator is God, who makes the wondrous things just listed or whatever He wills; the noncreator makes nothing, great or small. The comparison rebukes idolatry by denying any likeness between God and idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r1.anchor: ما ذكر من المخلوقات البديعة أو يخلق كل شيء يريده

ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r2.claim: The fāʾ after the interrogative hamza directs the denial to the supposed inference of likeness from God's preceding mighty acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r2.anchor: وتعقيب الهمزة بالفاء لتوجيه الإنكار إلى ترتب توهم المشابهة المذكورة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r3.claim: Creation is singled out from the preceding acts because it is their greatest and clearest instance, or because each preceding act is itself a particular creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r3.anchor: والإقتصار على ذكر الخلق من بين ما تقدم لكونه أعظمه وأظهره

ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r4.claim: Although one might expect the negative comparison first, the chosen order respects possession's precedence over absence and stresses that shirk lowers lordship to the level of inert matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r4.anchor: وكان حق الكلام بحسب الظاهر في باديء النظر أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق لكن قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r5.claim: The noncreator may mean all noncreating beings, intelligent and inanimate, with من favoring rational beings; alternatives are intelligent beings alone with idols inferred a fortiori, or idols alone, but Alusi prefers the broader reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r5.anchor: والمراد بمن لا يخلق كل ما هذا شأنه من ذوي العلم كالملائكة وعيسى عليهم السلام وغيرهم كالأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r6.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r6.claim: Idols fall under the denial either directly or by an a-fortiori inference: if even intelligent noncreators are unlike God, inert idols are still less comparable.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r6.anchor: ودخول الأصنام في حكم عدم المشابهة إما بطريق الإندراج أو بطريق الإنفهام بدلالة النص

ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r7.claim: Alusi notes that the verse is used to refute the Muʿtazilite doctrine that human beings create their own acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p117/r7.anchor: واستدل بالآية على بطلان مذهب المعتزلة في زعمهم أن العباد خالقون لأفعالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r1.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r1.claim: Al-Shihab allows the universal scope of creates to come from treating the verb as intransitive, and says the verse then cannot refute the Muʿtazilite claim that people create acts, since universal negation permits particular affirmation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r1.anchor: وقال الشهاب بعد أن قرر تقدير المفعول عاما على طرز ما ذكرنا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r2.claim: Alusi suspects the transmitted passage may be corrupt; otherwise he regards its denial of the verse's argument against the Muʿtazila as a lapse by al-Shihab.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r2.anchor: ولعلها سقيمة وإلا فلا أظن ذلك إلا كبوة جواد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r3.claim: The phrase asks why people do not notice and recall what is already clear, needing only recollection of something previously conceived and then forgotten.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r3.anchor: أي ألا تلاحظون فلا تتذكرون ذلك فإنه لجلائه لا يحتاج إلى شيء سوى التذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r4.claim: Some supply عدم المساواة as the omitted object of remember, then treat remember as an explicit metaphor for knowing because there was no earlier conception to recall.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r4.anchor: وقدر بعضهم المفعول عدم المساواة وذكر أنه لعدم سبقه حتى يتصور فيه حقيقة التذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r5.claim: One account makes the metaphor explicit in the estimated object; another makes it implicit there and treats the assertion of remembering as its imaginative elaboration.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p118/r5.anchor: الاستعارة مكنية في المفعول المقدر وإثبات التذكر تخييل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r1.claim: The one who creates is God; the one who does not create is the idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r1.anchor: {أفمن يخلق} يعني: الله تعالى، {كمن لا يخلق} يعني الأصنام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r2.claim: The question calls people to recognize the difference between God and idols.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r1.claim: The question denies equivalence after proofs of God’s power, wisdom, and exclusive creation; one unable to create cannot share His divinity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r1.anchor: إنكار بعد إقامة الدلائل المتكاثرة على كمال قدرته وتناهي حكمته

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r2.claim: The expected comparison would ask whether the non-creator equals the Creator; reversing it highlights that idolatry makes God seem like powerless created beings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r2.anchor: وكان حق الكلام أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق، لكنه عكس تنبيها على أنهم بالإشراك بالله سبحانه وتعالى جعلوه من جنس المخلوقات العجزة

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r3.claim: Those who do not create include every being worshipped besides God, rational beings or idols; they are treated as rational because called gods, or for stylistic matching and emphasis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r3.anchor: والمراد بمن لا يخلق كل ما عبد من دون الله سبحانه وتعالى مغلبا فيه أولو العلم منهم أو الأصنام

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r4.claim: They should recognize the error because it is so evident that slight recollection and attention suffice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:17/r4.anchor: فإنه لجلائه كالحاصل للعقل الذي يحضر عنده بأدنى تذكر والتفات

DURR-FULL:v5p119/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p119/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p119/r2.claim: Qatada says God is the Creator and Provider, whereas the idols worshipped besides Him create nothing and can neither harm nor benefit their worshippers.
DURR-FULL:v5p119/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق} قال: الله هو الخالق الرازق وهذه الأوثان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r1.claim: After evidence that God alone creates and that this entails benefaction and gratitude, the two clauses draw the conclusion and rebuke the polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r1.anchor: على انفراد الله بالخلق ابتداء من قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r2.claim: The rhetorical question denies any equality between creator and noncreator; the comparison targets the polytheists' treatment of idols as God's partners and shows who merits divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r2.anchor: أي لا يستوي من يخلق بمن لا يخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r3.claim: Since the noncreators meant are idols, the normally rational relative pronoun man is used by matching the wording of man who creates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r3.anchor: وحين كان المراد بمن لا يخلق الأصنام كان إطلاق من الغالبة في العاقل مشاكلة لقوله أفمن يخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r4.claim: The question rebukes the polytheists for turning away instead of reflecting on the denied equality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p123/r4.anchor: مستعمل في الإنكار على انتفاء التذكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r5.claim: The verse confronts them with the distinction between the one who creates and originates things and those unable to do any such thing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r5.anchor: ثم قررهم على التفرقة بين من يخلق الأشياء ويخترعها وبين من لا يقدر على شيء من ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r8.claim: The challenge continues by rebuking them with ‘will you not reflect?’

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r1.claim: The one who does not create refers to idols; the polytheists treated them as if they had reason and discernment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r1.anchor: يعني الأوثان وإنما عبر عنها ب من لأنهم نحلوها العقل والتمييز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r2.claim: The address challenges the polytheists to take heed as the believers did.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r2.anchor: يعني المشركين يقول أفلا تتعظون كما اتعظ المؤمنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains that man is grammatically possible for the non-creator because it is paired with the creator, just as it can cover a human and an animal when they are mentioned together.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437/r3.anchor: قال الفراء وإنما جاز أن يقول ( كمن لا يخلق ) لأنه ذكر مع الخالق كقوله ( فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين )

JISHUMI:v6p4011/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4011/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4011/r3.claim: Although idols are inanimate, the verse uses the rational relative form because it speaks of creation, an act of rational agents, or because worshippers treat idols as rational.
JISHUMI:v6p4011/r3.anchor: أنه ذكر الخلق، وهو من فعل العالم. وثانيها: أنه على تقدير ما يعقل لعبادتهم له.

JISHUMI:v6p4011/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4011/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4011/r18.claim: God, who creates, is not equal in worship to idols, which create nothing and neither benefit nor harm; the question calls people to reflect.
JISHUMI:v6p4011/r18.anchor: أفمن يخلق: يعني الله سبحانه في استحقاق العبادة والإلهية كمن لا يخلق يعني الأصنام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r1.claim: The creator is God and the one who does not create is the idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ أفمن يخلق ﴾ أي الله تعالى ﴿ كمن لا يخلق ﴾ أي الأصنام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r2.claim: Man, normally for rational beings, is used because the idolaters named and worshipped idols as gods; alternatively, the comparison first means one rational creator is unlike a rational noncreator, much less an unintelligent object.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r2.anchor: وجىء بمن الذي هو لأولى العلم لزعمهم حيث سموها آلهة وعبدوها فاجروها مجرى أولى العلم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r3.claim: The wording reverses the surface expectation to refute idolaters who equate idols with God: by making idols God's equals, they make God like created things, so the verse denies that a creator resembles a noncreator.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r3.anchor: وانما لم يقل أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق مع اقتضاء المقام بظاهره إياه لكونه الزاما

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r4.claim: The verse is an argument against the Muʿtazila concerning the creation of acts.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r4.anchor: وهو حجة على المعتزلة في خلق الأفعال

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#3/r5.claim: The closing question urges them to recognize the error of their position.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r1.claim: The one who creates is God, while those who do not create are the idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أفمن يخلق } هو الله تعالى. { كمن لا يخلق } يريد الأصنام.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r2.claim: Idols neither create nor harm nor benefit; the creator is more entitled to worship than created things that cannot help or harm.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r2.anchor: ومعنى الآية: من كان قادرا على خلق الأشياء المتقدمة الذكر كان بالعبادة أحق ممن هو مخلوق لا يضر ولا ينفع

QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r3.claim: The idols are referred to with the personal interrogative من because Arabs speak of them as persons when worshipping them; compare the question about their limbs in 7:195.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r4.claim: Another explanation for من is its proximity to the pronoun associated with the Creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r4.anchor: وقيل: لاقتران الضمير في الذكر بالخالق.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ compares this usage to asking which is which when a rider and his camel are confused, although one is not human.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: هو كقول العرب: اشتبه علي الراكب وجمله فلا أدري من ذا ومن ذا وإن كان أحدهما غير إنسان.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r6.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawī says من may ask about the Creator, but ما asks about kinds, and God is not a member of a kind; Moses answered Pharaoh’s من-question but turned aside from the malformed ما-question.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r6.anchor: قال المهدوي: ويسأل ب «من» عن البارىء تعالى ولا يسأل عنه ب «ما» لأن «ما» إنما يسأل بها عن الأجناس

QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r7.claim: The creation argument is supported by the challenge to show what anyone besides God has created in 31:11 and 35:40.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:17/r7.anchor: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه [لقمان: 11] أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض [فاطر: 40].

RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r1.claim: After presenting the ordered signs as proofs of a wise Creator and explanations of His blessings, the passage rejects worship of anything besides Him, especially inert objects.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر الدلائل الدالة على وجود القادر الحكيم على الترتيب الأحسن والنظم الأكمل

RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r2.claim: The Creator of the listed things cannot be equated with beings unable to create anything; even basic awareness shows worship belongs only to the greatest benefactor, never to lifeless idols without understanding, power, or choice.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r2.anchor: والمعنى : أفمن يخلق هذه الأشياء التي ذكرناها كمن لا يخلق بل لا يقدر البتة على شيء

RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r3.claim: The non-creators are idols: inert beings, although min normally marks rational beings.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r3.anchor: المراد بقوله : { من لا * يخلق } الأصنام ، وأنها جمادات فلا يليق بها لفظة ( من )

RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r4.claim: One answer to using rational min for idols is that unbelievers called them gods and worshipped them, so they are grammatically treated like rational beings.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r4.anchor: الوجه الأول : أن الكفار لما سموها آلهة وعبدوها ، لا جرم أجريت مجرى أولي العلم

RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r5.claim: A second explanation for min is stylistic matching with the preceding min in the phrase about the Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r5.anchor: والوجه الثاني : في الجواب أن السبب فيه المشاكلة بينه وبين من يخلق

RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r6.claim: A third answer means the Creator is unlike even non-creating rational beings, much more unlike idols; the question about idols' limbs shows their inferiority to living people, not that such limbs would make them worthy of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11/r6.anchor: أن يكون المعنى أن من يخلق ليس كمن لا يخلق من أولي العلم فكيف من لا علم عنده كقوله : { ألهم أرجل يمشون بها }

RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r1.claim: Although an objector expects the comparison to be reversed, the wording stresses how impossible it is to equate the maker of immense benefits with contemptible, inert things in naming, worship, and reverence.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r1.anchor: والجواب : المراد منه أن من يخلق هذه الأشياء العظيمة ويعطي هذه المنافع الجليلة

RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r2.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r2.claim: Some of al-Rāzī's associates infer that servants do not create their own acts: if creating anything made a being divine, humans who create acts would also have to be gods, which is false.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r2.anchor: احتج بعض أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن العبد غير خالق لأفعال نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r3.claim: The Muʿtazilites answer that the verse contrasts the Creator of the heavens, earth, humans, animals, plants, seas, stars, and mountains with beings unable to create anything; this does not address a servant's acts.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r3.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الجواب : عنه من وجوه : الوجه الأول

RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites also say the verse establishes that a creator is superior to a non-creator and should not be equated with one in worship, but it does not make every creator a god.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r4.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الجواب : عنه من وجوه : الوجه الأول

RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r5.claim: Their analogy is that a person with working legs is better than an idol unable to walk and should not worship the inferior idol; this does not make the person a god, just as creating alone does not imply divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v20p11#2/r5.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الجواب : عنه من وجوه : الوجه الأول

STUDYQURAN:16:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r1.claim: After describing nature's benefits created by God, the verse challenges worship of lifeless idols instead of their Creator.
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r1.anchor: Following the mention in the preceding verses of natural phenomena, which God has created for the benefit of human beings

STUDYQURAN:16:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r2.claim: The one who creates nothing refers to the idols of the Makkan idolaters; the verse rebukes equating them with the Creator and worshipping them as gods.
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r2.anchor: The one who creates not is a reference to the idols worshipped by the Makkan idolaters

STUDYQURAN:16:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r3.speaker: Ashʿarite theologians
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r3.claim: Ashʿarites argue that “Creator” and creation properly belong only to God; human acts, like all things, are created by God.
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r3.anchor: Ashʿarite theologians adduced this verse to indicate that the title “Creator,”

STUDYQURAN:16:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r4.speaker: Some Muʿtazilites
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r4.claim: Some Muʿtazilites allow “creating” in a limited sense for humans with intelligence and agency, while stressing that powerless idols cannot create and should not be worshipped.
STUDYQURAN:16:17/r4.anchor: Some Muʿtazilites responded by saying that the verse does not deny that the act of “creating,” in a limited sense

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r1.claim: The closing verses of the preceding argument summarize its detailed case and infer divine oneness: God alone creates, bestows innumerable blessings, knows the hidden and open, owns all, and governs all.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r1.anchor: تقرير إجمالي للحجة المذكورة تفصيلا في ضمن الآيات الست عشرة الماضية واستنتاج للتوحيد وهي حجة واحدة أقيمت لتوحيد الربوبية

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r2.claim: The integrated proof is directed against polytheists who deny God’s sole lordship, not against people who deny a creator.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r2.anchor: فمجموع ما تتضمنه الآيات من حديث الخلق والنعمة والعلم مقدمات لحجة واحدة أقيمت على توحيد الربوبية الذي ينكره الوثنية

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the claim that the passage establishes tawhid through two independent proofs, creation and blessing: creation alone proves a maker and unity in creating, not exclusive lordship over polytheists.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r3.anchor: يظهر فساد ما ذكره بعضهم أن الآيات تثبت التوحيد من طريقين طريق الخلقة وطريق النعمة

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r4.claim: The polytheists already accepted God as creator of everything, even their idols, while claiming idols received delegated control of the world and intercession; creation alone would not answer that claim.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r4.anchor: لا ينكرون وجود الصانع ولا أن الله سبحانه خالق الكل حتى أوثانهم

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r5.claim: The creation argument establishes that God alone is the true benefactor: all beings and the benefits arising from them belong to Him as absolute, inalienable ownership.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r5.anchor: إذا كان الله سبحانه خالقا لكل شيء موجودا له كانت آثار وجودات الأشياء وهي النعم التي يتنعم بها له سبحانه

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r7.claim: The rhetorical question denies equality between God and what others invoke; its interrogative form expresses repudiation.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r7.anchor: ونفي للمساواة، والاستفهام للإنكار، والمراد بمن لا يخلق

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r8.claim: Those who do not create are the deities people invoke apart from God.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r8.anchor: والمراد بمن لا يخلق آلهتهم الذين يدعونهم من دون الله

TABATABAI:16:17-19/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r9.claim: God continuously creates things and therefore owns their existence, effects, particular systems, and the universal order; He cannot equal one who creates nothing.
TABATABAI:16:17-19/r9.anchor: فإنه تعالى لخلقه الأشياء يملك وجوداتها وآثار وجوداتها التي هي الأنظمة الخاصة بها والنظام العام الجاري عليها

TABRISI:16:17-18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:17-18/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:17-18/r3.claim: The verse asks whether the creator of all things deserves worship like idols that create nothing; equating them is manifest error.
TABRISI:16:17-18/r3.anchor: معناه أفمن يخلق هذه الأشياء في استحقاق العبادة والإلهية كالأصنام التي لا تخلق شيئا

TABRISI:16:17-18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:17-18/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:17-18/r4.claim: Man is used of non-rational things because the clause follows mention of creating.
TABRISI:16:17-18/r4.anchor: وجعل من فيما لا يعقل لما اتصل بذكر الخلق

TABRISI:16:17-18/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:17-18/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:17-18/r5.claim: The address urges idolaters to reflect and recognize their flagrant error.
TABRISI:16:17-18/r5.anchor: أي أفلا تتذكرون أيها المشركون فتعتبرون وتعرفون أن ذلك من الخطأ الفاحش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the creator is God and those who do not create are the idols mentioned in this surah, as in the statement this is God's creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ما ذكر في هذه السورة، ومن يخلق هو الله عز وجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r2.claim: Al-Farra explains the use of man for idols by their association in the sentence with the Creator; Arabs similarly pair a human rider with his camel under man.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: والعرب تقول: اشتبه علي الراكب وجمله، فلا أدري من ذا ومن ذا؟ حيث جمعها وأحدهما إنسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r3.claim: Another view says the idols are addressed as man because people worshiped them, just as a verse asks whether idols have feet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنهم لما عبدوها ذكرت بلفظ (من) (¬4)؛ كقوله: {ألهم أرجل} الآية [الأعراف: 195]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the question addresses the polytheists: will they not take heed as the believers did?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد المشركين، يقول: أفلا تتعظون كما اتعظ المؤمنون (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi's associates argue that the verse establishes one Creator, distinguished from creatures by the power to originate creation; one who claims to create his own acts makes himself God's partner in creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r5.anchor: قال أصحابنا: وهذه الآية دليل على أن الخالق واحد، وإنما يتميز الخالق من المخلوق بالقدرة على اختراع الخلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r6.speaker: أهل التأويل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r6.claim: Exegetes say the verse denies that creator and noncreator can be treated equally in worship, just as one should not give equal thanks to a benefactor and a non-benefactor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p37/r6.anchor: وقال أهل التأويل: معنى هذه الآية: إنكار تشبيه من يخلق بمن لا يخلق بالتسوية بينهما في العبادة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r1.claim: The creator is God, mentioned earlier in the surah; the noncreator is the idols.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r1.anchor: { أفمن يخلق } يعني: ما ذكر في هذه السورة، وهو الله تعالى { كمن لا يخلق } يعني: الأوثان.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r2.claim: The question asks whether creator and noncreator are equal and deserve equal worship; it calls people to take heed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:17/r2.anchor: يقول: أهما سواء حتى يسوى بينهما في العبادة؟ { أفلا تذكرون } أفلا تتعظون كما اتعظ المؤمنون.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r1.claim: The non-creators are idols; God and the idols worshipped besides Him are unequal because idols control neither harm, benefit, death, life, nor resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r1.anchor: لا يستوي الله والأوثان التي تعبدون من دونه، التي لا تملك ضرا ولا نفعا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r3.claim: The address is to the polytheists; the believers are the ones who take heed.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r4.claim: Qatāda says God is the Creator, while the idols worshipped besides Him create nothing.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p56/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: {أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق} [النحل: 17] الله هو الخالق،

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r1.claim: The primary audience is the pagan Arabs of Muhammad's time, and the idols are meant: the question invites them to reason through the evidence of God's oneness, creative power, and favors and reconsider their beliefs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r1.anchor: Allah’ın varlığına, birliğine, yaratıcı kudretine, geniş lutuf ve merhametine işaret eden yukarıdaki âyetlerin muhatapları öncelikle Hz. Peygamber dönemindeki putperest Araplar olduğu için onların putları kastedilerek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r2.claim: God's blessings exceed those already recalled; the reminder of forgiveness and mercy in verse 18 is as important as material gifts and offers hope to those who recognize the Creator and believe despite their past errors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r2.anchor: 18. âyetin sonunda Allah’ın bağışlayıcılığının ve merhametinin özellikle hatırlatılması, hem bunların yukarıdaki maddî nimetler kadar önemli olduğu anlamını taşımakta hem de insanlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r3.claim: Even if people outwardly appear to believe, they are warned that God knows every hidden and open state if they retain old errors, ill will toward Muslims, or hostility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:17/r3.anchor: eğer dıştan inanmış gibi görünmelerine rağmen içten eski yanlış inançlarını, müslümanlara karşı kötü niyetlerini, düşmanlık duygularını sürdürmeye kalkışırlarsa Allah’ın gizli açık her türlü hallerinden kesinlikle haberdar olduğunu da bilmeleri gerektiği uyarısında bulunulmaktadır

BURHAN:v4p412/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p412/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p412/r1.claim: The uncreating referent may be idols, described with the rational relative man because Arabs treated them as objects of worship.
BURHAN:v4p412/r1.anchor: والذي لايخلق المراد به الأصنام لأن الخطاب مع العرب

BURHAN:v4p412/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p412/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p412/r2.claim: Alternatively, man covers all beings worshiped besides God, rational and nonrational, using the rational form by predominance in a mixed group.
BURHAN:v4p412/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد ب من لا يخلق العموم الشامل

BURHAN:v4p412/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p412/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p412/r3.claim: In an example listing crawling creatures, man applies to snakes and animals because rational and nonrational referents mix, so the rational form predominates.
BURHAN:v4p412/r3.anchor: فعبر بها عمن يمشي على بطنه وهم الحيات وعمن يمشي على أربع وهم البهائم لاختلاطهم مع من يعقل

BURHAN:v4p412/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p412/r4.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v4p412/r4.claim: One explanation says ma is more common because nonrational things and their grammatical contexts are more numerous; man is reserved for the less common rational cases for stylistic fit.
BURHAN:v4p412/r4.anchor: قيل إنما كان من لمن يعقل وما لما لا يعقل لأن مواضع ما في الكلام أكثر من مواضع من

BURHAN:v4p412/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p412/r5.speaker: الإبياري
BURHAN:v4p412/r5.claim: Al-Ibyari says the man/ma distinction applies to relative pronouns only, not conditionals, which require a verb and do not govern nouns.
BURHAN:v4p412/r5.anchor: ذكر الإبياري في شرح البرهان إن اختصاص من بالعاقل وما بغيره مخصوص بالموصولتين

BURHAN:v4p412/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p412/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p412/r6.claim: The relative man can take a singular verb by form and a plural predicate by meaning, as in the wording about those who are Jews or Christians.
BURHAN:v4p412/r6.anchor: فجعل اسم كان مفردا حملا على لفظ من وخبرها جمعا حملا على معناها

ITQAN:v3p118/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p118/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p118/r2.claim: Although the apparent comparison is reversed, it answers idolaters who made non-creators like the Creator through excessive worship, treating idols as the norm; the response mirrors their distorted ordering.
ITQAN:v3p118/r2.anchor: فإن الظاهر العكس لأن الخطاب لعبدة الأوثان الذين سموها آلهة تشبيها بالله سبحانه وتعالى فجعلوا غير الخالق مثل الخالق

BURHAN:v4p56/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p56/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p56/r4.claim: من is used for idols, although ما is normal for nonrational things, because the audience treats the idols as deities; the author answers that the wording aims to make the intended target clear to them.
BURHAN:v4p56/r4.anchor: وكان أصله كما لايخلق لأن ما لمن لايعقل بخلاف من

BURHAN:v3p427/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p427/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p427/r3.claim: The reversed question confronts idolaters on their own terms: since they elevate non-creators as gods, it applies the stronger argument by lowering the sacred Creator rather than raising the deficient idols.
BURHAN:v3p427/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنهم لما قاسوا غير الخالق خوطبوا بأشد الإلزامين وهو تنقيص المقدس

BURHAN:v3p427/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p427/r4.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v3p427/r4.claim: Al-Sakkākī says ‘who does not create’ means a living, capable creator, indirectly rejecting any comparison between idols and God a fortiori.
BURHAN:v3p427/r4.anchor: قال السكاكي وعندي أن المراد ب من لا يخلق الحي القادر من الخلق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r9.claim: A Qur'anic sense of خلق is forming or shaping, as in forming from clay and the contrast between idols and their makers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخلق في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه
